title: Return doubled elixir
prompt: Define double_elixir(amount) returning twice its input. Example: double_elixir(3) returns 6. Do not only print it.
tests:
assert double_elixir(3) == 6, "double_elixir(3) should be 6 (3 elixir doubled)"
assert double_elixir(0) == 0, "Zero doubled remains zero"
assert double_elixir(2.5) == 5, "Fractional input 2.5 should return 5"

title: Afford cards by name
prompt: Implement can_afford(card, elixir) with teaching costs X-Bow 6, Tesla 4, Skeletons 1. Unknown names return False. Example: can_afford("Tesla", 4) is True.
tests:
assert can_afford("Tesla", 4) is True, "Tesla is affordable at exactly 4"
assert can_afford("X-Bow", 5.9) is False, "5.9 is below the X-Bow cost"
assert can_afford("X-Bow", 6) is True, "X-Bow is affordable at exactly 6"
assert can_afford("Skeletons", 0) is False, "Skeletons still needs one elixir"
assert can_afford("Skeletons", 10) is True, "Skeletons is affordable at ten"
assert can_afford("Unknown", 10) is False, "Unknown cards must not be treated as free"
hint: Return early for a name absent from the mapping.

title: Regenerate with a default
prompt: Implement regenerate(elixir, seconds, multiplier=1) using the continuous 2.8-second model and cap ten. Inputs are nonnegative. Example: regenerate(3, 2.8, 2) returns 5.0. Add a docstring describing the units.
tests:
assert abs(regenerate(3, 2.8) - 4) < 1e-9, "Default 1x should add one in 2.8 seconds"
assert abs(regenerate(3, 2.8, 2) - 5) < 1e-9, "2x should add two in 2.8 seconds"
assert regenerate(9, 10, 3) == 10, "Regeneration must cap at ten"
assert regenerate(4, 0) == 4, "Zero elapsed seconds must preserve elixir"
assert regenerate.__doc__, "Include a docstring describing the returned quantity"
hint: Put the multiplier in the gain formula and min around the total.

title: Apply toy tower damage
prompt: Implement damage_left(hp, damage) returning max(0, hp-damage). Example: damage_left(300, 500) returns 0. Inputs are nonnegative.
solution:
def damage_left(hp, damage):
    return max(0, hp - damage)
tests:
assert damage_left(300, 100) == 200, "100 damage should leave 200 of 300 HP"
assert damage_left(300, 500) == 0, "Overkill should leave zero"
assert damage_left(300, 300) == 0, "Exact lethal damage should leave zero"
assert damage_left(300, 0) == 300, "Zero damage should preserve HP"
hint: Use the earlier arithmetic rule inside a reusable function.

title: Cycle a four-card hand without mutation
prompt: Implement cycle_hand(hand, queue, slot). Inputs are two four-card lists and slot 0-3. Return (new_hand, new_queue). Replace the selected slot with the front queued card; append the played card to the queue. Preserve both inputs. Example: playing X-Bow in slot 0 with Skeletons at the queue front draws Skeletons and queues X-Bow last.
solution:
def cycle_hand(hand, queue, slot):
    new_hand = hand[:]
    new_queue = queue[:]
    played = new_hand[slot]
    new_hand[slot] = new_queue.pop(0)
    new_queue.append(played)
    return new_hand, new_queue
tests:
h = ["X-Bow", "Tesla", "Ice Wizard", "Knight"]
q = ["Skeletons", "Tornado", "Rocket", "The Log"]
h_before, q_before = h[:], q[:]
nh, nq = cycle_hand(h, q, 0)
assert nh == ["Skeletons", "Tesla", "Ice Wizard", "Knight"], "Slot zero should draw the queue front"
assert nq == ["Tornado", "Rocket", "The Log", "X-Bow"], "Played X-Bow must go to the queue end"
assert h == h_before and q == q_before, "Do not mutate either input list"
assert nh is not h and nq is not q, "Return independent outer lists"
nh, nq = cycle_hand(h, q, 3)
assert nh == ["X-Bow", "Tesla", "Ice Wizard", "Skeletons"], "Slot three must work too"
assert nq[-1] == "Knight", "The actual played slot supplies the queued card"
for step in range(4):
    nh, nq = cycle_hand(nh, nq, 3)
assert nh[3] == "Knight", "After four further ordinary plays, Knight should return"
assert len(nh) == len(nq) == 4, "Both collections should stay four cards long"
hint: Copy with slices before pop or assignment; return two values separated by a comma.
